chapter: Split, hospital and decline of tap
title: Tap dancing as daily prayer in the hospital
summary: Green denies being dejected, says he was getting back to the people, and tapped daily as self-preservation, performing family shows on Long Island.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Did you feel yourself not quite feeling that playfulness at this time, sort of dejected?
No.
Loss of appetite, things like that?
(Laughter)
Well, I mean, these things --

Well, you see, I was at a place where happiness was needed again, you see. I called myself getting back to the people. I know there are shut-ins that have to be treated to a performance -- they'd have to come -- they was brought to where the performances were performed by the attendants, see, and they had sporting events, you know, like tournaments
like that, you know. Sort of semi-olympics, you see. So, I was very happy, you know. I was getting good reports, you know. (Recording interruption)
What you're basically talking about here is the activities that you used to do in the hospital?
I started teaching myself again.
So, for a while there at the hospital you were very inactive at the beginning.
Yeah, well, I mean, they have to decide on where they want you to to be resident, you know, see.
(unintelligible)
Did you tap dance while you were at the hospital?
Oh, that was a daily prayer.
Was it another way of going into the wood shed, in a way?
Yes, well, it was. I mean, self-preservation.
You were still developing tap -- you didn't just give up?
No, it would have been too disrespectful, you see. Oh, you're still going on with it, yes. By all means.
I'm taping it.
Yeah, well, see, at that place up in Long Island, you know, they had family shows. And tome that, I think, that's the height of anyone's personality, you see.
(End of tape #16
